claims.statement: `GET /api/admin/export/dataset` is the only export entrypoint: `registerExport` registers `GET /export/dataset` inside the `/api/admin` plugin scope, so the admin auth guard runs as a `preHandler` hook, and the handler always answers with the assembled dataset as a raw JSON attachment (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="komyuter-dataset.json"`, `Content-Type: application/json`) rather than the `{ success, data | error }` envelope.

`readExportRows` gathers the whole dataset with seven independent `SELECT`s — routes, fare_configs, directions, stops, detours, detour_stops, restrictions — executed in one `Promise.all`, with no `ORDER BY` at any level and no `is_active` filter, projecting every geometry column through `asGeoJSON` (`ST_AsGeoJSON(col)::jsonb`) so rows already hold GeoJSON objects.

The seven reads run as separate statements outside a transaction, so assembling the export is not a single atomic snapshot of the tables and a concurrent write is not reflected consistently across parents and children.

`buildExportDataset(rows, exportedAt)` is a pure builder that groups children by foreign key into maps (`stopsByDirection`, `detourStopsByDetour`, `detoursByDirection`, `restrictionsByDirection`, `directionsByRoute`) and nests them under their parent, so child `direction_id`/`route_id` columns never appear in the document and a parent without children gets an empty array.

Within a direction the base `stops` array is explicitly sorted ascending by `stop_order`, while routes, directions, detours, detour stops, restrictions and fare configs keep the unordered order Postgres returned — the export integration test works around that by locating a base direction through its `terminals.origin` rather than by array index.

Detour stops are a separate collection with their own `detour_stop_id` namespace: the document emits them only inside `detour.detour_stops`, never in the direction's base `stops` chain, and the assembler does not sort them by `stop_order` (unlike the entity loader, which orders detour stops by `stop_order`), so the consumer must order them itself.

Every document opens with `schema_version` (`EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, currently "1.1"), `coordinate_order` (`EXPORT_COORDINATE_ORDER`, "lng_lat") and an `exported_at` produced by `assembleExportDataset` via `new Date().toISOString()`; both constants are shared `typeof` literal types, and the zod mirror pins them with `z.literal(...)`.

`coordinate_order: "lng_lat"` is a self-describing contract for the external consumer rather than a configuration knob: every embedded GeoJSON pair is `[longitude, latitude]` per ADR-0013, and the JSON Schema the integration test enforces hardcodes the value with `const`, so a document whose marker disagrees with the constant fails validation.

`fare_configs` is the only place the document converts types: those five numerics are drizzle `numeric(...)` columns with no number mode, so `readExportRows` types them `unknown` and `buildExportDataset` maps each through `num()` (`Number(value)`), which is why a stored `"13.00"` / `"1.80"` pair serializes as the JSON numbers `13` and `1.8`.

`referenceCheck(dataset)` returns human-readable problem strings and covers exactly three referential faults: a direction origin or destination terminal that names no stop in the document (null terminals are skipped), a `detour_id` equal to some direction id, and a `stop_id` equal to some direction id.

The id sets `referenceCheck` compares against are dataset-wide unions rather than per-direction lists, so a terminal pointing at another direction's stop is not reported, and stop-versus-detour id collisions, `detour_stop_id` collisions, `fare_config_id` existence and restriction index bounds inside the polyline are not checked at all.

The invariant that each direction's terminals resolve inside its own stop list is created by the write path, not by the check's scope: the pair save sets each member's `origin_stop_id`/`destination_stop_id` to the first and last stop rows it just inserted for that direction (with a comment naming the export reference check as the reason), and the export integration test asserts it for both the base and the derived return.

`referenceCheck` has no production caller — only the unit test imports it — and the route calls `assembleExportDataset` alone, so a document with a dangling terminal or a colliding id is served as a 200 download instead of being rejected.

A null `routes.color` is normalized to the empty string by the assembler because the enforced JSON Schema requires `color` to be a required string while the shared TypeScript type and its zod mirror both allow `null`.

The document carries a curated subset of columns: `is_active` appears only on routes and directions, and `direction_kind`, `ar_marker_enabled`, stop `notes` and all timestamps are dropped, so a consumer cannot tell from the document which member of a pair is the server-derived return.

Because `DELETE /api/admin/stops/:stopId` and `DELETE /api/admin/restrictions/:restrictionId` are soft (`is_active = false`) and the export neither filters on nor emits that flag for those entities, a deactivated stop or restriction is still exported and is indistinguishable from a live one in the document.

An empty database is not an error: the endpoint still returns 200 with a schema-valid document holding `routes: []` and `fare_configs: []`, and the latency suite additionally requires 19 of 20 export reads under one second.

No arrival-time data can reach the document: the export types carry no ETA/arrival/departure field, and both the unit and integration tests assert the serialized dataset contains none of those keys (ADR-0009).

The admin Export page is still a placeholder while the server endpoint is live: `pages/Export.tsx` renders a "Nothing to export yet" empty state even though `/export` is wired in the router and the nav sections, and nothing under `apps/admin` calls `GET /api/admin/export/dataset`; `docs/ADMIN.md` tracks wiring it as roadmap item R7.

Changing the document surface is a coordinated change: the spec JSON Schema at `specs/001-local-supabase-backend/contracts/export-dataset.schema.json` sets `additionalProperties: false` at every level and is what the Ajv helper in the test suite validates against, so a field added to the assembler without a matching schema entry fails the suite, and bumping `EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION` also requires editing the hardcoded `const` there; the shared zod `exportDatasetSchema` is not referenced by any module.
